response.summary: The revision resolves F1–F7 as written. The ground is now painted full-bleed through route-guarded html/body :has. All five rail separator ranges are listed, with gap 0. Every row gets the same row geometry and an inside stripe. The 18px/16px mobile padding is stated explicitly. The ledger shadow is replaced entirely. Exact tones are given and the top light stops at 220px. I found one material problem left. The rule for the stronger seven-column day edges is defined only by the calendar being wider than 36rem. But seven-column mode actually depends on both the media ranges and the container width. A Home-scoped day border would also outrank the transparent-border resets in the existing list-mode media and container rules. So list-mode days would get borders at 721–999px, and at enlarged text. There is also one low-severity contrast margin worth recording.

findings.evidence: Decision 6 says to use '#bcc4b5 day edges in seven-column mode (week container>36rem)' and to keep the unframed days in list mode. In the stylesheet, seven-column mode happens only when two conditions both hold. First, a media range must set 7 columns: ≤1279 (line 388) or ≤720 (line 422). Second, the `.week` container must not hit `@container(max-width:36rem)` (lines 464-466). List mode is set by the media rules at ≤999 (lines 409-410) and ≤640 (lines 427-428), by the container rule, and by the >1279 default. All of these reset `.day{border-color:transparent}` at specificity 0,1,0. Example: at 800px the media rule gives list mode, but the full-width `.week` is about 700px, which is more than 36rem. A rule like `@container(min-width:36.01rem){main[data-route=home] .day{border-color:#bcc4b5}}` would match, and its 0,2,1 specificity would beat the `transparent` reset at line 410. List days would then show framed tiles, which contradicts the plan. The same thing happens at >1279 if the edge is set unconditionally. The 200% text cases change which mode applies, because 36rem then means 1152px.
findings.fix: Define the edge condition as both conditions together, not container width alone. Put the Home day-edge rule inside `@media (max-width:1279px) and (min-width:1000px), (max-width:720px) and (min-width:641px)` and nest an `@container (min-width:36.0625rem)` inside it (Edge supports nesting). Alternatively, add Home-scoped `border-color:transparent` resets in every list-mode range at the same 0,2,1 specificity, placed after the edge rule. Have surfaces.cjs record the computed `.day` border colour at 1366, 1048, 800, 700, 390 and 320, at normal and 200% text, and check it against the column count.

findings.evidence: The coach/session rail is now #e0e2db (relative luminance about 0.754). That is darker than the Home ground #e6e7e2 (about 0.795; ΔL* about 1.8, so the rail reads as recessed). Several items in the rail use `--muted` #616660: `.message-meta time` (line 174), `.count` (line 107), `.quiet` 'Eastern time', and `p` text in general (line 32). By my calculation these come to about 4.6:1 on the rail. That passes 4.5:1, but only just, and it is the lowest-margin text on the page. The plan lists 'controls losing contrast on a darker neutral ground' as a risk but sets no threshold for text contrast on the rail.
findings.fix: Add a check to surfaces.cjs: computed contrast of muted, metadata and text-button colours against their actual parent background (rail, ground, sheet). Require at least 4.5:1, and record the values. If a sample falls below this, darken muted text inside the rail with a Home scope, or lighten the rail slightly.

coverage: Re-checked round-1 findings F1–F7 against the revised decisions 1–6. Each is addressed in the plan text.
Re-read the style.css breakpoint and container-query rules for `.desk-side`, `.days`/`.day` (lines 384-473) to test the revised separator ranges and day-edge condition against existing specificity.

Checked index.html: `main#main` holds only route content. `#modal` and `#drawer` dialogs are outside `main`, so `main[data-route=home]` rules don't reach dialogs. html/body :has only changes the page background behind them.
Checked app.js sessionCard: `.prep-preview` appears only when `state.note` is set. Checked desk-side markup: coach card then session card. These support the rail and preview decisions.
Calculated approximate luminance and L* by hand for #e6e7e2, #e0e2db, #f7f4ee and #616660.
